description: Use this to read or quote an EU legislative provision, such as PSD2 Article 97 or RTS-SCA Article 5. Returns the source text of an article, annex or recital as markdown, with its cite anchor, provenance and text state; a long provision paginates by structural block. version_id is optional, and a pinned version id is refused with the URL where that text is published. include_correspondences adds the cross-instrument article equivalences. cites and terms_used list what the returned text cites in other acts and the defined terms it uses, with the call that opens each.

cursor.description: Continue a paginated provision. Bound to the release.

include_correspondences.description: Off by default. When true, an article carries correspondences[]: the cross-instrument article equivalences the corpus publishes, each with the counterpart's own get_provision locator, version and cite anchor. null means the release predates the mapping table, not that the article has none.

instrument_id.description: Registry id of the instrument, e.g. "psd-2".

annex.description: Annex number, roman or arabic ("I", "1"); omit for an instrument whose single annex is unnumbered.

kind.description: Which kind of provision the locator names.

paragraph.description: Numbered paragraph within the article, e.g. "2".

point.description: Lettered point within the paragraph, e.g. "b".

on_date.description: ISO date; returns the provision-level applicability view.

version_id.description: Omit, or pass "current", for the served text. A pinned version id returns version_not_served with the URL where that text is published.

name: get_provision

cites.description: What the returned text cites in other acts, in source order, one entry per target. phrase is the text's own wording before the citation. outcome says what this service can open: served (open returns the cited provision), parent_served (open returns a parent; find cited_limb in it), act_only (the text names only the act; get_instrument shows coverage, not what any article says), not_served or not_held (nothing here opens it; check it at source_url or the official text), or unresolved. Open a target when its wording could change the answer. An empty list means no citation was extracted from this text, not that nothing outside this corpus is relevant.

correspondence_coverage.description: The instrument pairs the correspondences cover, older instrument first, and what a missing entry means.

partial.description: true where the correspondence covers only some paragraphs of the two articles; false where it covers them as a whole; null where the release does not record it or the data cannot show which.

relationship.description: amended_from or supersedes, the analysis layer's own vocabulary, or their mechanical inverses amended_into and superseded_by.

annex.description: Annex number, roman or arabic ("I", "1"); omit for an instrument whose single annex is unnumbered.

kind.description: Which kind of provision the locator names.

paragraph.description: Numbered paragraph within the article, e.g. "2".

point.description: Lettered point within the paragraph, e.g. "b".

correspondences.description: An annex or a recital carries an empty list. A mapping this service will not serve is omitted and correspondence_withheld names the instrument and the reason, so a short list is never silently under-claimed.

follows_part.description: The bar follows the closing subparagraph of the paragraph in `follows`.

precedes_part.description: The bar precedes the closing subparagraph of the paragraph in `precedes`.

deletions.description: Deletions marked on the whole provision, in source order. A EUR-Lex deletion stub names the act that deleted what stood there: "within": the nth "—————" in the provision text; "after": something deleted after this provision (a whole article or chapter), with `heading` naming the Title, Chapter or Section heading it stands under when one comes between them; "title": in its heading. A record with source "council_compromise" is a ▌ the Council compromise text prints on a line of its own where it deleted a point, paragraph or passage: `follows` and `precedes` name the items it stands between ("after": at the end of the provision text, precedes null, with `heading` as for a stub), `follows_part` or `precedes_part` says that side is the paragraph's closing subparagraph; `page` and `source_url` give the page of the Council document that prints it; the provision text carries no mark for it. The record says where the bar stands, not what was removed, and compare_versions does not show it. Mechanically derived from the source; not part of the legal text. Null means no record is served for this provision (see the typed warning), never that nothing was deleted.

headings.description: The headings of the divisions the provision sits under, outermost first.

mapping_basis.description: The recorded reason behind verified_no_successor or withdrawn, verbatim; null for every other state.

mapping_state.description: Present when include_correspondences is true. On an article of an earlier instrument whose correspondences to its successors are recorded: mapped, a successor is recorded; verified_no_successor, an editorial record says it has none; unresolved, not yet mapped, which is not a finding that it has no successor; withdrawn, an earlier mapping was withdrawn. null on any other provision or where the release predates the field. A correspondence shows where a provision went, not whether its obligation changed.

markdown.description: The provision's source text as markdown. A sub- or superscript with no Unicode form is inline <sub>/<sup> (K<sub>IRB</sub>); one with a Unicode form uses it (m²).

pointers_omitted.description: Entries left out of cites and terms_used by the size limit. Request a paragraph or point to see them.

complete.description: All notes referenced in this response's text, not the whole document or later pages.

source_notes.description: Null means unverified/unsupported coverage or an older release; consult the typed warning. Not an empty note inventory. Legal content_hash and block counts exclude this attachment. The verified note scope is DMD articles and recitals. Introductory citations are not an MCP provision kind: their notes remain on the website's reading pages, not attached to articles.

terms_used.description: The instrument's own defined terms in the returned text that lead somewhere, each with its definition's cite. leads_to lists the provisions the definition refers to, already followed. includes lists categories defined as kinds of this term, and kind_of the categories this term is a kind of, so a provision that applies to those applies to it too; both are read from the definitions, nearest first. An entry with a condition is a category made by a scope article, and the link holds only when the condition, quoted from its cite, is met; for names which of the term's categories an entry concerns. A term absent here may still be defined: get_defined_term returns any definition.

title.description: Plain text: a script with a Unicode form uses it, one without reads flat (KCCP).

title_path.description: Plain text: a script with a Unicode form uses it, one without reads flat (KCCP).

topics.description: Discovery tags, assigned by rules from phrases in the provision's headings, title and text, or set for the whole instrument. They can miss a provision and can reflect a passing mention.

title: Read EU legislative provision
